title: Nonpayment Cancellation of HVAC Maintenance Agreements
content:
On HVAC Maintenance Agreements, membership fees are due on their billing period start, and an agreement is cancelled for nonpayment only once a fee has stayed unpaid beyond the 30-day grace period.

## The rule

1. Fees are due on their billing period start, and the oldest unpaid one is the monthly or annual membership fee charge with the earliest billing period start that is not fully paid, payments being applied oldest first.
2. An agreement is cancelled for nonpayment only when a fee remains unpaid more than 30 calendar days after the fee's due date; the count starts the day after the due date.
3. A nonpayment cancellation carries no admin fee and no refund, unused visits lapse, and fees billed for periods before the cancellation remain owed.

The due dates and payments are read from the agreement's billing record.

## Counting the grace period

The day after the due date is day 1. On day 30 the fee is unpaid for 30 days, which is not more than 30; from day 31 it is unpaid for more than 30 days.

| Due date (hypothetical) | Date checked | Day of the count | Fee still unpaid | Nonpayment cancellation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 April | 1 May | 30 | Yes | Not yet; the fee is not more than 30 days unpaid |
| 1 April | 2 May | 31 | Yes | The condition is met |
| 1 April | 2 May | 31 | No, paid in full on 28 April | Not met for this fee |

## Finding the oldest unpaid fee (hypothetical)

Monthly membership fees of 31.95 are due on 1 March, 1 April and 1 May, and 40.00 has been paid in total. Applied oldest first, the payment settles the 1 March fee and 8.05 of the 1 April fee. The oldest unpaid fee is therefore the one due on 1 April, and its grace period is counted from 1 April.

## Effects of a nonpayment cancellation

| Item | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Admin fee | None |
| Refund | None |
| Unused visits | Lapse |
| Fees billed for periods before the cancellation | Remain owed |
